# Chapter 0: Preface

There is a certain special quality of life when you are close to people who love you. These people make life worth living, and act as a sanctuary; a protection from the adverse outside forces that try to tear you apart. From humble beginnings, an elf, a plant, a poltergeist, and an arsonist worked together to make their way in the universe, doing odd jobs and completing missions. What kept them the closest together, however, was their harboring of the galaxy's most targeted prisoner: a goat. While this goat was not particularly special, he had the special statistic of being the last known member of his species. This kid underwent many ups and downs, fighting for his survival against assassination and ignorance. Now, however, lies the end of their combined journey, a matter of life or death.

# Chapter 1: The Intervention

On the planet of Vega-5, the Vortox Pummelers vacationed with great goals in mind. While they were there to relax, Garrick and Sanya pushed for an intervention for Emmett, wanting to explain to him how he needed to stay strong in his fight against grass. There were no real plans for the other crew members, but Garrick mentioned that he wanted them to have a "[Grand ol' summer of sixty-nine]{Garrick}", whatever that meant. At least Seth understood, anyhow, as he motioned the others over to the lazy river to relax.

Although it was their main point for the vacation, the intervention was not entirely interesting. Garrick, Emmett, and Sanya rested along the coast of the river, making sure to stay away from the others. The ghost was adorned in a floral-patterned vest and bandana, the goat in a pair of heart-speckled trousers (gifted to him by Jess one not-so-sober night), and the plant in a tightened, black swimsuit. Upon adjacent pool chairs, the conversation between them was continuous and undisturbed—a perfect setting for privacy.

"[How are you holding up, big guy?]{Garrick}" Garrick asked. The rays from his tanning reflector made Emmett feel euphoric, the heat being reminiscent of his home planet's climate.

"[Yeah… This hits the spot. Thanks for taking me here, by the way.]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Emmett had a soft smile beneath his sunglasses, nearly drifting off.

"[Emmett, don't fall asleep just yet. We need to talk to you.]{Sanya Dreadflower}" Sanya placed a hand on his arm, clenching into its soft texture. The Squoatling raised his head attentively. "[We're proud of you for making it this far.]{Sanya Dreadflower}"

"[What do you mean?]{Emmett Tawfeek}"

"[With your recovery—]{Sanya Dreadflower}"

"[Your grass addiction]{Garrick}," Garrick butted in. "[You've gone a long way from your self-endangering tendencies and—]{Garrick}" The ghost stopped when Sanya motioned that this was not the best approach. Emmett's smile faltered after hearing this.

"[I mean, I'm doing it for Squoat, not just myself. Whatever gets me closer to another Squoatling as soon as possible]{Emmett Tawfeek}," Emmett expressed as he rested his horns against the twine of the seat. "[As soon as he gives me the coordinates, I might get back on it.]{Emmett Tawfeek}"

"[Isn't he listening to you right now?]{Sanya Dreadflower}" Sanya was a tad paranoid of potentially angering a god.

"[He hasn't responded to me in what feels like semesters, despite my requests. Honestly, it's starting to feel that he's not a god, but rather a living, mortal being.]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Garrick rolled his eyes as he heard this. Clearly there were no immortal beings in the galaxy, much less gods; only special cases and tendencies, like Seth.

"[Regardless of Squoat, we need you to stay off the weed.]{Garrick}" Emmett sighed, tilting the reflector closer to him. Sanya was a little aggravated by Garrick's lack of sensitivity. She was once influenced by Dread, anyhow.

"[Emmett, I don't know whether you know how much we love you. Although we each joined the VP in our own ways, you were there for all of us. You're the foundation of our crew.]{Sanya Dreadflower}" She shrugged. "[Being such an important part of our lives, I cannot possibly let you…]{Sanya Dreadflower}" Emmett tipped his sunglasses, showing his sickly orange-yellow eyes.

"[Die? From the galaxy's perspective, I'm as good as dead. I have no purpose in living for anyone but you guys. My biological family is dead. My species is dead. I'm as good as—]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Sanya clenched his arm harder, causing him to stop.

"[Isn't it enough to be loved by your family? You cried when I died on the ship GUYs ago. You felt alive then, and you felt a reason to survive despite the Llamanians, despite Dread, and despite my death. We're not being selfish in wanting you around, are we? Otherwise, I would've never come back.]{Sanya Dreadflower}" Emmett slouched within his seat.

"[I guess you're right.]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Garrick handed him a milk-based margarita, presumably leaving during Sanya's speech. Emmett took a sip from it reluctantly, having never tasted one before.

"[Look, man, I'm not really one for speaking seriously here, but everything Sanya's said is true. You mean a lot to us. Plus, who said that the Squoatlings are dead? Didn't Squoat tell you that he knows where another is?]{Garrick}" Garrick floated above him. Emmett took larger sips, having enjoyed the drink.

"[He did, but I feel like he's dragging me on here. He probably doesn't know.]{Emmett Tawfeek}" He shrugged his shoulders and relaxed back in his seat. After a significant silence and contemplation, Emmett sighed, looking up towards the sun. "[I promise to not touch grass again. It gives me bellyaches anyways.]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Sanya let go of him, feeling accomplished.

"[Good boy]{Sanya Dreadflower}," Sanya jested. Garrick suddenly grabbed onto Emmett's bottom hooves, dragging him out of his seat.

"[We need to baptize him in his decision, help me out.]{Garrick}" This startled Emmett, causing him to hold onto his seat tightly.

"[No, no, I'm good!]{Emmett Tawfeek}" By the time he cried this out, Sanya had already grabbed a hold of him and yanked him out of his seat.

"[Sayonara!]{Sanya Dreadflower}" A large splash occurred immediately after, leaving the two giggling at a wet, irritated goat.

# Chapter 2: The Interception

On 1-22, 3020 GUY, disaster struck for the Vortox Pummelers. Deep within space, far away from the nearest civilization, the Slingshot lost power. This was uncommon, but of little alarm to the crew—they knew how to survive in such a situation. Used to the continuous lull of the ship's engine, the majority of the crew awakened upon the loss of power. Emmett and Dakari, however, slept through the incident.

"[Shit. Holograms are dead!]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" screamed an angry Seth. He was about to finish another lustful dream, only for it to be cut off. He stormed out of his block towards the engine.

"[Seth, calm down. You're going to wake up the others]{Garrick}," mentioned Garrick. This was a futile statement, as when Seth does not get what he wants, he will go through hell and back to make it known.

"[Fuck off, ghost. I need to check the engine.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" Seth opened up the fuel compartment to notice that it was empty. Of course it was. There was always a bullshit reason. "[I guess I should have paid for our orbital fueling subscription. Oh fucking well.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" The elf switched his comms to everyone, making sure to blare his announcement. "[WE ARE OUT OF FUEL AND IN DEEP SPACE. PREPARE FOR A LONG TIME WITHOUT POWER.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" Emmett turned to his other side within his sleep, somehow not waking up.

"[Greeeeeat. Just wonderful]{Sanya Dreadflower}," sarcastically moaned a certain plant. As time continued, the serenity of deep space was too much for the crew. Sanya began to bash her head against her doorway, unable to teleport to the temple. Some rooms, including Emmett's, were completely locked up given the lack of electricity, leaving those within stranded. Even Garrick was moderately upset, given that he could not entertain anyone nor bother them. Depression ensued, leaving most of the crewmates bored and without purpose. Emmett woke up, however, when the ship jostled greatly, flipping it on its side. Emmett fell out of his bed, slamming against his door.

"[Fuck! What the hell is this?]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Emmett swiftly dodged Dakari; the porcupine's quills surely would have killed him otherwise.

"[Huh? Emmett, what did you do?]{Dakari}" Dakari was stuck upon a corkboard in their room.

"[I didn't do this! Why is it so dark?]{Emmett Tawfeek}"

"[Just turn the lights on, idiot!]{Dakari}" Dakari reached for the switch, unable to get to it from his position. Emmett lay prone on the wall, flipping the switch repeatedly.

"[Guys, we're out of power in our—]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Emmett was interrupted by another jostle, this time lighter, but with a continuing vibration.

"[WE KNOW. HAVE YOU SERIOUSLY BEEN ASLEEP THIS WHOLE TIME?]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" screamed an infuriated Seth. Emmett swallowed, a little intimidated by Seth's anger.

"[Yes, we have… Can you look outside for me?]{Emmett Tawfeek}" The goat kept his limbs flat on the wall in case of another flip. Coincidentally, the ship was hit again, pushing it upside down. Dakari fell off the corkboard, luckily nowhere near Emmett.

"[I am not enjoying this…]{Dakari}" muttered the porcupine.

"[How about I just fuck your mom again?]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" Seth sighed over the comms, really just annoyed at Emmett as he spoke.

"[Why do you have to bring this up again?]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Emmett put his hoof to his scrunched-up face.

"[I'm going to penetrate both of you if Seth doesn't check the window and tells us what's out there]{Sanya Dreadflower}," Sanya angrily interjected. Emmett shivered as he thought of this. How would she even attempt such a thing?

"[Fine. I'll do it.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" Seth slowly eased his head to his right and looked out the huge window. In his vision was a large spaceship, with a tractor beam aimed at them! They were saved!

"[A ship's saving us!]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" This did not make much sense to Emmett, as no one in the Galactic Union usually bothers to give each other a hand, especially in deep space.

"[Seth, can you make out the name of the ship?]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Seth squinted his eyes and read the bold text that scrolled along the side of the ship's hull.

"[The Almighty… Lla… Confederate…]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" Seth paused for a second. "[Shit, Emmett, they're after us!]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" Emmett started to hyperventilate a little. Why was it so hard to cope with death now that he was going to face it? He had already taken on the Llamanian mothership in person and survived. He previously said that he didn't care if he died, but then again, that was when he was depressed. The goat had so much to think about in so little time!

"[W-What do w-we do?]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Emmett stammered, inching to a corner of the ceiling. The tractor beam shot the Panty Slingshot, dragging it in towards The Almighty.

"[We need to arm ourselves. We won't go down without a fight.]{Sanya Dreadflower}" Sanya was first to answer, as Seth was still trying to devise a plan of sorts.

"[Wish I still had my ribbons]{Iris}," Iris sighed, pulling her dagger out of her skirt pocket. She began to regret giving those away; with so little control over her fire powers, there wasn’t much she could do. Emmett began to scale his wall, trying to reach his bed so he could grab his Maggo-Pistol.

"[For the Vortox Pummelers!]{Dakari}" Dakari shouted, feeling patriotic as he took out his vials of lethal fluid. The other members of the crew interchangeably shouted "For the VP!" and "For Emmett!" as they began to arm up. As Emmett grabbed his pistol, Seth began a short speech.

"[My friends, it's been an honor to work with you for all of this time. I don't know what I'd do without Emmett, since he's like a son to me, and I don't know what I'd be without you guys to back me up.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" There were audible attempts to hold in laughter or interjections over the communicators as he finished this statement. "[However, we're fighting against innumerable odds here. And you guys know I can't gamble without me rigging something up. I don't have anything set up, so it's possible that some of you, if not all of you will die here. I don't mention me as I'm pretty much immortal. I will make sure to honor you guys if you die, but I will try my best to prevent it from happening to any of you. Just remember though, in my eyes, Emmett’s life comes before all of yours.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" There were mixed responses, with some feeling uneasy, others irritated, and still others hopeful. The ship suddenly stopped, and the hatch to the ship creaked open.

"[To your stations!]{Sanya Dreadflower}" Sanya ordered, despite no one having any stations to attend to. They simply hid throughout the ship, while Emmett and Dakari sat behind their dresser. A slew of steps were overheard boarding the ship, causing the entire ship to vibrate. Clearly the intruders were armed to the teeth and prepared for any assault.

"[Come out with your hands, nubs, hooves, or whatever's on your limbs up! We know you killed Richard Jamerez! We know you're harboring a Squoatling!]{Llamanian Commander}" boasted a large, burly commander. Emmett felt his heart start to beat at a ridiculous rate. This was it. Life or death.

"[You'll have to get through me first!]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" Seth jumped out into the opening, holding a larger-than-life plasma cannon, a RYNUS-3500K in particular. This weapon was capable of taking out massive mobs, breaking through armor and muscle as if they were butter. The commander stood mightily within his power suit, disregarding the threat. Inside, however, he quivered, having never seen such weaponry in his twenty-four GUYs of commanding.

"[Put it down, Seth. We both know you're the only man that has any capability of putting a dent in our plans.]{Llamanian Commander}" Seth's arms shook as he took aim, clearly intimidated. How did they know his name? Did they know he was immortal too? How much did they know of the other members? After a strong breath, he returned to his senses, or lack thereof.

"[I don't care. Now fucking die.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" As soon as he pushed this out, he pulled the trigger of the RYNUS, exploding the entire entryway. The Llamanians were all blasted away, excluding the commander. Surprisingly, while his armor was completely desecrated, the commander remained untouched. Seth dropped the RYNUS, expecting that all of his adversaries would have been blown away. "[Fight me like a man.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" He took his fists out, having a spare pistol within the back of his pants. He just needed the right moment.

"[Fine. Have it your way.]{Llamanian Commander}" The commander dropped his gun, taking out his armored fists. Even without weapons, this was clearly an uneven match. He inched closer to the elf, ready for anything. Seth waited for the commander to strike, but his expectation was not met. They were both waiting for the right moment. "[Come on, Seth, not even going to cheat me out of this?]{Llamanian Commander}" The commander, impatient, slammed into Seth's gut. Withstanding the punch, Seth took out his pistol and fumbled with the trigger. A brutal mistake, as the Llamanian took his other fist and crunched Seth's armed hand, breaking it quickly. Seth had little time to react as the commander began to dent his face in with his fist, eventually killing him.

Sanya noticed Seth's failure and reacted, hopping atop the commander with her Dreadsword. She swiped at the Llamanian's neck with quick efficiency; however, the commander was still prepared. Just as the sword met his fur, he was able to grab the blade and toss it away. Sanya was now defenseless, and as she tried to grab something from Dread, her opponent fell backwards, crushing the floran into unconsciousness.

"[I'm going to need spectral backup, pronto.]{Llamanian Commander}" The commander stared into Seth's dead eyes as he awaited the poltergeist to come in. Two more Llamanians boarded the ship, cloaked in reflective gear and armed with spectral stun darts. As expected, Garrick and Iris arrived, with Iris almost completely engulfed in flames and Garrick armed with… nothing?

"[I'm not going to fight—]{Garrick}" Garrick was interrupted by the crazy-ass firewitch. She ran up to the commander and fired a blast of eternal damnation. Near instantaneously did he burst into flames.

"[Fire! Fire!]{Llamanian Commander}" he cried, and almost immediately the commander was shot with a huge flame retardant. While he expected fire, clearly he was not thinking Iris would be so quick to act. Now much more intimidating, the commander grabbed Iris, extinguishing her with the help of the others. To end her suffering, he headbutted her, leaving her limp, nearly lifeless, and branded. "[Now, what were you saying, ghost?]{Llamanian Commander}"

Garrick eyed the injured body of his friend. "[Now look. We can reason here]{Garrick}," the ghost sputtered out as he edged closer to the brigade, trying to think of an effective item to take out.

"[Reason? Three of your friends are dead and you want me to reason with you?]{Llamanian Commander}" The commander was lying through his teeth, as only one of them was dead, but he needed to keep to the plan.

"[Well, sir, I don't want any more of them to get hurt. I'll do anything.]{Garrick}" Garrick was right in front of the commander, his hand nearing his vest inconspicuously. They both lied to each other's faces.

"[Anything?]{Llamanian Commander}" The Llamanian was genuinely curious about this trick, but he kept his caution. Right as he asked this, Garrick took out an unholy hand grenade and pulled its pin. He winked and started to fly away from the scene. The Llamanian practically jumped within his heavy suit, shocked.

"[SHOOT AND SCATTER!]{Llamanian Commander}" he screamed. The two cloaked Llamanians shot at Garrick, missing a few times, but eventually hitting their target. They kicked the grenade outside to protect the unconscious crewmates and followed the commander in his dash into the depths of the ship.

"[Man, this stinks]{Garrick}," Garrick muttered to the camera before passing out from the dart’s fluid.

There were only a few members left, and only one that really mattered to the infiltrators. They passed through Pummelers' hallway, making note of their various framed photos strewn about the 1950s-styled halls. [*They must really care about the Squoatling*]{Llamanian Commander}, the commander thought. [*It's a shame it had to come to this.*]{Llamanian Commander} He stopped for a moment at a picture of Emmett as a youngling. Memories began to flow through him, bringing him back to the days of old, when the Llamanians and Squoatlings were close friends. It hurt him deeply to have murdered so many innocent people, particularly ones he had known for most of his life. Next to the picture was a hatch labeled "Emmett". How convenient.

The commander and the two others were clearly not strong enough to burst through a five-inch-thick adamantium hatch, so he called for an electrician to power up the ship, allowing them entry into the room after a few minutes of the ship booting up. The room, for the most part, was trashed, as was the rest of the ship from the gravitational surge they experienced. The fur and quills that littered the floor were unappealing to say the least, but it gave a clue that he was still alive. Oh, and that he was in the room still. After a bit of searching through his and Dakari's privacy, the closet moaned.

"[Emmett, are you there?]{Jessica}" muttered Jess, who apparently was knocked out, within the closet, and forgotten about by Emmett. Great boyfriend material, am I right? Emmett shook, causing the dresser to wobble ever so slightly. His cover was quickly blowing away, and Dakari was quick to notice this.

"[Have some of this!]{Dakari}" Dakari threw a venom-serrated quill at the commander's head. However, his aim from behind the dresser was not so sharp, causing him to impale one of the other Llamanians. Butterfingers. The commander grabbed Dakari from behind the dresser, somehow not noticing the Squoatling next to him. All the porcupine could do was chuckle. "[No hard feelings, eh?]{Dakari}" He was immediately slammed to the ground, causing some of his quills to shoot out from his back and onto the floor. Just like the others, he was instantaneously knocked out. The other cloaked Llamanian opened the closet and was tackled by a fierce Ottori woman.

"[Take this!]{Jessica}" She mauled his face with her claws, giving her time to take out a dagger and stab him repeatedly. The tackle, however, caused the Llamanian to land atop Emmett's arm, breaking it with the sheer force of steel hitting bone. Emmett cried loudly, unable to withstand this pain. As the Squoatling teared up, Jess was smacked off of the Llamanian corpse, breaking a few of her teeth as she fell to the floor.

"[There you are]{Llamanian Commander}," the commander muttered as he pushed aside the dresser, revealing to him a sobbing, miserable goat with an arm pinned to the floor.

"[Why… are you doing this to us…?]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Emmett managed to get out as his breath got heavier. The commander stared at him with a deep sigh. Why did it have to be this way? He had to harm yet another innocent being for loyalty. For his people. He picked up his fallen brother, allowing Emmett to take his disfigured arm to himself. The goat stared at it, mortified, perceiving its unnatural orientation as a symbol for his body in a few seconds. "[Just take me, man. You've already ruined my life enough already. You've ruined everything.]{Emmett Tawfeek}" The Llamanian frowned as he took a rifle out.

"[Sorry. Orders are orders. I hope you understand.]{Llamanian Commander}" He took the rifle and flipped it, hitting Emmett with the butt end with just enough force to knock him out. [*Lla, why did things have to be so difficult?*]{Llamanian Commander}

# Chapter 3: The Interaction

## Penthouse Reasoning

"[Wake up, Emmett.]{Llamanian Scientist}" The Squoatling was nudged repeatedly by the Llamanian scientist, hoping to get his attention. They had quite a busy schedule ahead, and there was little time for slacking around. After about a minute, the Llamanian stroked Emmett's right horn, resulting in the Squoatling reflexively thrusting his legs out to kick.

"[Don't touch me there, Seth—]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Emmett widened his eyes as he eyed his environment, clearly surprised. He turned to the seat he was bound to, observing the elegant designs and golden rims of the throne. Was he dead? "[Where am I?]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Emmett stammered slowly.

"[Don't you recall what happened yesterday?]{Llamanian Scientist}" The Llamanian eyeballed his subject, curious whether he had amnesia of sorts. He was knocked out severely by the butt of the commander's rifle, and in tandem with his broken arm, it was likely that his body was more focused towards alleviating his pain over his memories. Strange, Squoatlings could be.

"[I think? I remember we were in a losing fight for the most part…]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Emmett muttered as he looked down at his casted arm. It hurt him to move the appendage in any direction. Clearly the Llamanians were not interested in doctoring his arm just yet, as the cast was a little flimsy. [*Standard procedure for a prisoner of war*]{Emmett Tawfeek}, he supposed.

"[Seth was killed, Garrick was sedated…]{Llamanian Scientist}" the scientist trailed off as he read off of a list of names. "[Sanya was knocked into an unconscious submission, Dakari was brutally injured and knocked out…]{Llamanian Scientist}" This list was making Emmett a little upset. How could they have been beaten so easily when they defeated larger armies with little resistance?

"[I get it, I get it. You beat us… And for some reason you're storing your reward in a penthouse, so-to-speak. Don't you guys want to kill me? I've accepted my death already. Just get it over with—don't be cruel.]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Emmett tried to pull his arms out of the binds to no avail. The researcher scribbled some notes on the clipboard, recording his patient's psychological responses.

"[Emmett, we don't want to kill you. We want to help.]{Llamanian Scientist}" This response surprised Emmett even more, causing him to struggle with greater intensity.

"[If you want to help me so badly, then... Get me out of this chair! Release my friends! Leave me alone!]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Emmett's requests left the scientist unfazed.

"[Not until you listen and you're calm.]{Llamanian Scientist}" Emmett rolled his eyes in defense—he did not want to listen to an irrelevant reason as to why he was bound up. "[Mr. Tawfeek. A large portion of the Llamanian population has regretted and detested the eradication of your species—]{Llamanian Scientist}" Emmett interjected, given the scientist's lack of emotion.

"[Look, I understand you're oh-so-sorry about killing my family, my people, and my planet, but I can't take you seriously with your monotone voice. Is there anyone else that can tell me this? Or rather, can I just get the summary?]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Emmett mustered with an attitude. The scientist was taken aback, almost hurt by the Squoatling's comment. Nonetheless, he persisted.

"[Quiet down, I'm trying to get this done as soon as possible, and it's difficult to continue if you keep on interrupting]{Llamanian Scientist}," the Llamanian barked. Once again, Emmett simply rolled his eyes and shut his mouth—this was going to be a doozy. "[The entire reason we exterminated your species was due to both a misunderstanding and corruption. You see, the Llaman at the time, Scribbels, had an unexplainable hatred for Squoatling culture. We think it's due to his upbringing and lack of empathy, but his actions were quite uncharacteristic, even for him... He saw you as weak and powerless, which technically you were biologically, but he didn't see you as an equal, so-to-speak.]{Llamanian Scientist}" Emmett sighed loudly, feeling like he was getting a migraine from having to endure this.

"[Regardless, he was eager to look for ways to either cut our ties with Squoatopia or find a way to keep you under his thumb, hence his increasing demands for tribute and ridiculous requests. The mining operation mishaps, which, if you do not remember, was the result of a miscommunication, whereas some Squoatlings mined and took all of the valuables from our mine, was the straw that broke the flamgel's back.]{Llamanian Scientist}"

The scientist paused and took a deep breath while Emmett rubbed his wrists against his binds, only giving himself a minor case of rug burn. [*Anything to get me out of this situation*]{Emmett Tawfeek}, he thought, biting into his lip through the pain. "[Scribbels found out about the incident and was infuriated. Instead of calling your Squingling to express his concerns, he contacted him with the intention of war. Scribbels rallied up the best of the Llamanian military and launched an assault on Vortox-56. It took about a week, and that time shown within Squoatopia.]{Llamanian Scientist}" The second mention of his hometown made Emmett perk up throughout the droll reminiscence.

"[I remember that a lot of the city was being militarized, and a curfew was established, not that it mattered to me. Maybe we were preparing for war]{Emmett Tawfeek}," Emmett replied.

"[Exactly, and you all were little match for us. Too peaceful and with little defense. To be honest, you were lucky to have *only* met us for all of your existence.]{Llamanian Scientist}" Emmett slouched back again, not amused by his indirect insults. "[Scribbels had just finished work on our PlanetBuster™ technology and he tried it out on Vortox-56, vaporizing the Squoatlings—aside from you, of course.]{Llamanian Scientist}"

"[Are you telling me that you haven't found any other Squoatlings?]{Emmett Tawfeek}" The scientist didn't respond, not wanting to get this conversation off-track.

"[Anyhow, the Llamanians that didn't agree with his mentality eventually rose up and formed a resistance. At first it was small, requiring a lot of secrecy and careful planning, but eventually a successful coup d'état occurred, allowing for peace to be the mindset of the Llamanian Armada. This happened about four GUYs ago, right after you were drugged and used an escape pod off this ship. Essentially, your actions caused us to be what we are today.]{Llamanian Scientist}" Emmett grunted, unsure of what to think about this change.

"[I know that it's going to take a long time for our relations to heal back to what they were, but it's our new duty to ensure that happens.]{Llamanian Scientist}" As soon as the scientist finished this, he loosened the Squoatling's binds, giving him freedom once more. Emmett stood up from the throne, wincing as his broken arm brushed against its edges.

"[So we're on equal terms then]{Emmett Tawfeek}," Emmett spoke, holding his arm to himself.

"[As of now, we see ourselves as below you, Squoatling. Our avarice and gullibility caused us to break off our most valuable alliance we had. In short, our species has a symbiotic relationship with yours in… a way that could not be met.]{Llamanian Scientist}" The scientist took out a needle and wiped it with alcohol.

"[So, why did you fight us so many times? Why did you try to abduct me over these last few GUYs?]{Emmett Tawfeek}" The scientist edged closer to Emmett, towering over him several feet.

"[Well, after how much damage the Vortox Pummelers caused us during their raid, we could not afford to be diplomatic. Too many lives would be at stake if we did. Did you see how much damage Seth did alone before we killed him? About ten of our members were completely vaporized! And that was when we were ambushing you. Imagine what would happen if we simply tried to talk it out.]{Llamanian Scientist}"

"[That… makes a lot of sense, actually]{Emmett Tawfeek}," Emmett quickly muttered to himself.

"[Give me your arm]{Llamanian Scientist}," the Llamanian demanded, holding the needle. Emmett reluctantly submitted, trusting him with his broken appendage. The scientist unhooked Emmett's sling and injected the broken arm with the serum, piercing through the cast. The Squoatling winced as this happened, the pain almost making him tear up. There were a lot of emotions going on, and his arms were quite a vulnerable spot for him. "[Give your arm a few days and the bones should be fixed up, along with the bruised muscle.]{Llamanian Scientist}"

"[Thanks, doc]{Emmett Tawfeek}," Emmett sarcastically responded, sitting back in the throne as the Llamanian rehooked his sling for him.

A long silence prevailed as the scientist continued to record Emmett's mental state and his responses. None of this was particularly interesting information, but it was necessary for the Republic. He eventually left the room for a bit to send his data to a secretary, and afterwards, the researcher came back with some chocolate.

"[You like chocolate, correct?]{Llamanian Scientist}" Emmett nodded, still feeling bummed out. The Llamanian rested the candy in Emmett's open hoof and looked over at him. "[I hope you understand that we're going to keep you safe here after this.]{Llamanian Scientist}" Emmett bit into the chocolate, swallowing hard as the scientist finished his statement.

"[I don't think I can stay here for long, sir. The VP is my family]{Emmett Tawfeek}," he pleaded. The scientist sighed and took a seat in front of the throne.

"[Look, we're both interested in preserving your species, correct?]{Llamanian Scientist}" Emmett nodded, stuffing his mouth with chocolate. "[And to keep you safe in hopes of reproduction, we can't have you exploring the galaxy anymore. The entire GU is after you, from what it seems, and the American Dad Empire, while sympathetic, would probably not be passive either, despite our alliance.]{Llamanian Scientist}" Emmett thought for a while, keeping quiet as he finished the chocolate.

"[Are you telling me that you all believe in there being another Squoatling, potentially female?]{Emmett Tawfeek}" He felt a little embarrassed asking this, covering his face partially.

"[Even better, Emmett, we think we've found one. Of course it's only rumors, but there's a space station that's said to harbor one, outside of the GU's jurisdiction.]{Llamanian Scientist}" Emmett continued to think, hating the idea of leaving his crew. He spent most of his life with them, and having to leave them for his species's survival made him feel guilty, despite the necessity. After a bit, he had a request to make.

"[I'll stay with you guys, but only on the condition that I can see them again, and that they can come back to see me.]{Emmett Tawfeek}" The scientist tilted his head at the request.

"[Why, of course you can see them. In fact, they're just starting to wake up. We want you to be as comfortable as possible in this transaction.]{Llamanian Scientist}" The cold tone made Emmett shiver as they both stood, beginning the trip from an interrogation chamber in the Panty Slingshot to the mess hall, from family to Llamanian.

## Prison Drama

Sanya awoke with a start. Her breath was jagged, and her body sore. Her head was wrapped in a tight bandage, completely covering her flower. Her head pounding from the wrestling move earlier, she checked her surroundings. Hard floor, check, padded walls, check, arbitrarily high ceiling and entrance, check. Something felt familiar about being in this prison cell to her, as if she were back at her birthplace, abandoned and alone. She tried to shake off this feeling by observing the others, but it persisted in the back of her mind. Seth was against the back wall, banging his head forcefully on the wall.

"[You know, banging your head on the wall isn't going to solve anything. Plus, it's hurting my head more. Shut up and suck it up.]{Sanya Dreadflower}"

"[At least you didn't die.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}"

"[You've died millions of times and you're complaining about it now?]{Sanya Dreadflower}" Seth stopped the banging and started to rummage through his satchel.

"[God damn, where's the alcohol in this bitch. I need to get high or something. Prison sucks.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}"

"[They let you keep your satchel?]{Sanya Dreadflower}" This thought occurred to Sanya as she unwrapped the tight bandaging on her head.

"[I mean, they let us keep our clothes, didn't they?]{Dakari}" Dakari spoke after lighting a VAPOrette. "[They aren't killing us immediately for a reason, y'know.]{Dakari}" Seth balled his hand in a fist.

"[I knew I should've charged the RYNUS up before they boarded. That was like a tenth of its potential power.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}"

"[Well, hindsight is twenty-twenty]{Sanya Dreadflower}," Sanya muttered to herself audibly. Seth was in no mood to hear shit. He was killed and trapped in a box with people he did not necessarily like.

"[Sanya, you're supposed to be an assassin. What's up with that, huh?]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}"

"[I seem to be losing against people I really shouldn’t be. Like when you bested me before airlocking Emmett.]{Sanya Dreadflower}"

"[Oh, bringing that shit up again, huh?]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" Seth balled up his fist. "[You're lucky I'm not drunk again.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}"

"[Or what? You’ll airlock another person out of drunken rage?]{Sanya Dreadflower}"

Dakari got up from the throw pillow he slept on. “[Guys, cool it. Our situation is shitty enough as it is, let’s not kill each other, too.]{Dakari}” Seth folds his arms, staring at Dakari with piercing eyes.

"[You're not the leader of the VP, I, Seth Im'kink'i, am. Now get in your place hedgehog.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}"

"[What's a hedgehog?]{Dakari}" Before Seth could continue, Sanya butted in.

"[It was because of your leadership that we all got caught!]{Sanya Dreadflower}" Sanya was angry, not at Seth, but in general. She sighed worriedly. “[God, I hope Emmett is doing alright. There's no telling what they're doing to him.]{Sanya Dreadflower}" The group was quiet for a bit, thinking about their endangered friend. After a long silence, Garrick arose from his deep slumber.

"[Am I dead?]{Garrick}" Garrick yawned obnoxiously loudly. Sanya seized her head, some noise getting drowned out from her headaches. Everything felt fuzzy. Damn, that Llamanian hit hard.

"[Garrick, would you keep it down?]{Sanya Dreadflower}"

"[Tell your little friend to shut it and I'll stop. He's really annoying.]{Garrick}" No one understood what the poltergeist was talking about. It was then that Sanya identified the source of her headache: Dread, screaming from the impact of the Llamanian before. Garrick slid Seth’s satchel towards himself and tossed a Blumpberry right into Dread’s mouth, as they’d practiced, and Dread quieted down. "[Now, can anyone tell me where we are?]{Garrick}" Garrick circled around the perimeter for a moment, keeping an eye—and ear—on everyone. "[Is Jess alright? And do we have an eye on Emmett?]{Garrick}" Seth eyeballed the Ottori girl with a bit of contempt, but did not say anything.

"[Jess is asleep, Garrick. We're all stuck in this prison cell, presumably on the Llamanian Mothership]{Sanya Dreadflower}," explained Sanya. Garrick had the bright idea of leaving through the wall, but he bruised his face on the way out.

"[Ouchiwawa.]{Garrick}"

"[You honestly think they'd just let you out that easily? These walls are made of some impenetrable material given our tools]{Dakari}," Dakari sighed. The walls were closing in on him, and he was masking his frustration with forced irritation.

"[I don't see you doing anything about this, Mr. I Know Everything]{Sanya Dreadflower}," Sanya exhorted.

"[There isn't much in the room for us to go off of. Our tools are useless here.]{Dakari}" He tried to stab into the wall with his kunai to no effect. Madness was slowly ensuing amongst the crew, and it was evident that morale was significantly low. There had never been a situation the Vortox Pummelers could not get out of, but this seemed to break the pattern.

After a long, tension-filled silence, Iris woke up. She immediately seized in pain from the headbutt that knocked her out. Her head was also wrapped in bandages, and the sedative she was injected with was making her woozy. “[Ahh… where am I? What’s going on?]{Iris}” Iris rubbed her head, dazed.

“[You got headbutted pretty hard, not to mention the…]{Garrick}” Garrick tilted over to see the mark on her temple. “[...branding. Guess they went too hard on the drug?]{Garrick}” Garrick winced.

"[Where's Emmett?]{Iris}" The flamewitch peered about the cell, worried about her furry friend.

"[We’re in the dark here. Just sit tight and hold your head. We can't get answers right now.]{Garrick}" Garrick tried to console her, seeing as she was the most injured crewmate by far. The confinement and lack of info was causing Iris to freak out a bit.

"[I hate small spaces like this; why couldn’t they have put us someplace bigger? Does—?]{Iris}" Iris flinched in pain, holding her head which had twinged painfully. "[Ow, *fuck—* I think I need medical attention. And to get off this ship. Maybe I can melt the wall?]{Iris}" Sanya looked at the elf-demon as if she was insane. She was injured badly and she was attempting to escape the inescapable. The floran sighed in response, folding her arms.

"[Hold your horses there, Iris. We'll probably get answers soon. Come over here and get some rest.]{Sanya Dreadflower}" As soon as Sanya mentioned this, an announcement over a lone intercom in the far corner blared throughout the room.

"[SIT TIGHT, VORTOX PUMMELERS. THE REASONING WITH YOUR PRECIOUS CARGO IS ALMOST FINISHED.]{Mothership Intercom}" Seth raised an eyebrow, questioning the use of the term ‘precious cargo’ for a squoatling. Squoatlings were definitely rare, but not to be objectified. Especially if the object is your adopted child.

"[So that's where our pilot is! About to be executed surely!]{Dakari}" Dakari threw his hands up and crossed his arms in frustration. Groans and moans spread throughout the room.

"[Who knew Emmett was such an integral part of this crew?]{Garrick}" Garrick mentioned this with a bit of sarcasm. It had occurred to him that over time, the bounty hunting crew had transformed into a Squoatling preservation party. "[Huh. It just occurred to me that—]{Garrick}" Sanya immediately glared at the poltergeist in annoyance.

"[WE'RE OPENING THE ENTRANCE MOMENTARILY TO BRING ANOTHER OF YOUR CREW. IF YOU TRY TO ESCAPE, YOU WILL BE RESTRAINED AND LOCKED UP ALONE.]{Mothership Intercom}"

"[Another crew member? How did they get out of my pockets?]{Garrick}" quipped the ghost. The entranceway opened up and spawned none other than Victor Chomsky himself. He looked a tad ruffled up and he wore a grimace across his face. He was pushed into the cell, which, despite the hard flooring, did not harm him whatsoever. After he landed, he charged his right flame gauntlet and aimed somewhere towards the crew.

"[Why didn't you get my distress beacon, traitor!]{Victor Chomsky}" Garrick raised an imaginary eyebrow.

“[Well, that’s not the greeting I expected]{Garrick},” Garrick said, unfazed.

"[You didn't answer the question. I sent a distress beacon out about three semesters ago. I was trying to contact the ship and everything.]{Victor Chomsky}" Sanya sidestepped from the angered arsonist as he hit the wall of the cell. Garrick could not help himself as he noticed Chomsky's arm bounce off the wall cartoonishly.

"[I was too busy with your mom's ghost]{Garrick}," the poltergeist muttered.

"[Be serious for a second! After my gang seized the mafia, their people started to live among us back on Chromatin. We lived peacefully for about a GUY before the Llamanians, of all people, showed up and captured us. We've been imprisoned for weeks!]{Victor Chomsky}"

“[Why send a signal to us, though? We could’ve been anywhere in the galaxy.]{Garrick}” Garrick was a little annoyed by the accusation. He was just happy to see his old friend again. “[Clearly we were far out if we didn’t receive your signal.]{Garrick}” Chomsky lowered his flame gauntlet, confused.

"[Wait, you're telling me that the ship doesn't have intergalactic communicators?]{Victor Chomsky}"

There was a bit of silence amongst the crew, aside from Seth, who blurted out a loud, "[It's a vintage ship, dumbass, of course not!]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" The Chromatin was pissed. How could he have forgotten?

"[Why do you guys have a vintage ship in the first place? All ships need to have an intergalactic communicator for long-range distress receiving.]{Victor Chomsky}"

Garrick piped up, a little irritated. "[You do realize that we’ve been on the run from the Galactic Union Patrol for what feels like a GUY now, right? Screw galactic requirements.]{Garrick}"

"[Fair point, I guess.]{Victor Chomsky}" Chomsky slumped down to the ground and exhaled. "[So what, you’ve all been stuck here?]{Victor Chomsky}" Sanya sat back down, still wary of the reckless newcomer who tried to attack her.

"[Yes, we've been here for a while now. Just be patient, we should get news soon.]{Sanya Dreadflower}" A silence fell among the crewmates for a while, aside from various grunts and groans from stomachs and bodies alike. Sanya wrapped an arm around Iris and toyed with her hair, trying to keep her mind off of their droll situation. This was almost an unconscious decision, as when she noticed her hands, she immediately pulled them back, embarrassed. "[How childish of me]{Sanya Dreadflower}," the Floran muttered. As monotony reigned and time moved at a snail's pace, Volentina rose and fell back asleep, exhausted from the Llamanian encounter, despite not doing much to help out. Right when Sanya began to lower her eyelids, the intercom interrupted blaringly.

"[WE ARE READY TO ACCEPT THE VORTOX PUMMELERS IN THE CAFETERIA TO TEND TO THEIR CARGO. DO NOT LEAVE ON YOUR OWN ACCORD. PATIENCE IS NECESSARY.]{Mothership Intercom}" The doorway to the cell opened up once more after this announcement, and out came a few Llamanian soldiers. They were not the most excited to see the Vortox Pummelers, mostly due to their fallen comrades.

"[Come up, one by one. Spectres last. Try anything tricky and we blast you.]{Llamanian Guard}" One of the soldiers pressed a keypad outside the doorway, causing stairs to ascend from the wall. Sanya and Iris stood, trying to avoid being pushed by the stairway.

"[Finally. Where's my boy?]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" Seth stood up and dusted off his pants. He was ready to get out of here with Emmett, no matter how many casualties.

"[Just comply and come with us to the cafeteria.]{Llamanian Guard}" One of the soldiers entered the cell and grabbed Seth's arm, pulling him up the stairs. Seth was a little too heavy to be dragged, but he went along, hoping to find a Squoatling—or at least some hot women. The others followed one-by-one, too bored to disobey and be difficult.

# Chapter 4: The Interjection

The Vortox Pummelers trudged from hall to hall through the Llamanian mothership, scrutinized by its loyal security and soldiers. The crew received glares and cruel jeers by the Llamanians they passed, the offenders clearly upset by their actions. Generally, they were unfazed by these insults, but something unhinged inside of Seth when an angry Llamanian woman piped up from behind him.

"[Seth, it’s so great to see you detained after you KILLED my husband two GUYs ago. Oh, Lla, how do you sleep at night!? You murdere—]{Llamanian Widow}"

"[You're upset about the death of your boyfriend? What about threatening the extinction of an entire race!? What about—]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" Seth's tangent was interrupted by the swift slap of a nightstick on his back, getting him to straighten up and quiet down. "[Ow, shit!]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" Sanya, who was behind him, stifled a chuckle and tried to advise her lackluster captain.

"[Shut up, Seth. You're only going to make things worse for us. They're letting us see Emmett. Don't squander it.]{Sanya Dreadflower}"

"[Don't tell me what to do, bitch.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" Sanya rolled her eyes, clearly not getting to him. What was the point, anyways? Was she getting soft? She used to enjoy seeing Seth in trouble. Or was it Dread finally getting to her? The god had been awfully quiet for some time.

The cafeteria took little time to navigate to from the prison, yet Sanya's revelation made her feel leagues away from the rest of the crew. Garrick noticed her blank stare as they continued forward and nudged her.

"[You doing alright, Sunflower?]{Garrick}" The Floran snapped out of it, furrowing her brow.

"[My name is Sanya, ghost. And I'm fine. Quit bothering me.]{Sanya Dreadflower}" Garrick opened his mouth to snap back, but realized he would make things worse with a snarky comment. Instead, he waited for Jess to catch up, grabbing her hand as the group approached the entrance to the cafeteria.

"[No funny business, everyone. We're just here to keep the peace. The Squoatling's sat in the room ahead.]{Llamanian Guard}" The guards loosened up, edging to the sides of the entranceway while grasping their weapons. Chomsky eyeballed the two guards with ire, still not understanding why he was here. He strutted into the cafe without regard to the others, satisfied with at least having the freedom to roam around the gargantuan lunchroom.

"[Can I leave now? I don't really want to be included with these guys. Aside from Garrick, of course.]{Victor Chomsky}" The arsonist tapped his foot on the ground, uninterested.

"[Just sit down, Chomsky. They're not killing us yet.]{Sanya Dreadflower}" Sanya entered the room, eyeballing the massive chair in the center of the lunchroom. The chair faced away from the crew, emitting a villain-esque vibe to those viewing from afar. "[Yeesh, that's a bit creepy.]{Sanya Dreadflower}" She took a seat at one of the tables, morbidly curious at what awaited.

"[I personally don't know why they have this chair backwards, sorry. Can you maybe… Turn it around?]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Emmett voiced his concerns to the Llamanian servants, waiting for a second to face his comrades. "[You guys okay?]{Emmett Tawfeek}" A rush of relief fell through the Vortox Pummelers, causing many of them, including the captain, to lower their guards. The Squoatling was adorned in a gray jumpsuit signed with the Llamanian insignia, as well as a tiny crown from Burger Dictator. He looked nervous, despite seeing his family for the first time in a while. "[I hope they took good care of you. They have to me.]{Emmett Tawfeek}" He raised his cast, showing to the crew that the Llamanians were, in fact, caring for him.

Garrick stared at his doctored arm, confused. Weren’t the Llamanians supposed to be their enemy? Why were they treating Emmett so well—Garrick didn’t even expect him to be alive. "[Is this a trick? What’s going on?]{Garrick}" Garrick lifted his hand to his mouth, lowering to a whisper. "[Blink twice if they’re—]{Garrick}" Sanya glared once again towards the poltergeist, but turned back, facing Emmett.

"[Burger Dictator? I see they’ve really gone the full nine yards.]{Sanya Dreadflower}" The Floran rolled her eyes, leaning towards their pilot. Emmett chuckled, taking off the plasteel crown.

"[Yeah. They really have been trying to say they're sorry, even giving me silly regal stuff. They don't really have resources to spare, but they're trying to make amends.]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Emmett gave Garrick a half-smile, tilting his head a little. "[No, this isn't a trick, Garrick. This isn't the first time a llamanian spared me, anyhow.]{Emmett Tawfeek}"

“[Amends for what? The assault of our crew, the years of chase, or the extermination of your entire race?]{Sanya Dreadflower}” Sanya was obviously upset; the paradigm shift of the Llamanians just seemed too good to be true.

"[Well, Sanya. The Llamanians opposed us for a while, but that’s because a dictator took their empire in a different direction. If you remember, the squoatlings and the llamanians had an interspecies bond. And… That bond was never really broken, just some guy grew too powerful and well… You know.]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Emmett took a hoof out towards one of the nearby Llamanians, grasping their hand. "[I never hated Llamanians in the first place, anyhow. Just had a phase where my intentions were out of proportion. We would've all torn them to shreds if they tried to be diplomatic, anyhow.]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Seth nodded at this statement, acknowledging that he would, in fact, have torn them to shreds.

"[I still don't understand. We carried out a huge raid on them less than a GUY ago, why are they hunky-dory with us again?]{Garrick}"

"[They had a bit of a civil war and a coup d'état. They want to keep my species alive for cultural reasons.]{Emmett Tawfeek}" He nodded to the llamanian whose hand he was holding, letting go afterward. There was a sense of repressed sadness in his actions.

Seth approached to try and grab the kid, only to be barred away by those guarding him. "[My boy! I’m just glad you’re safe.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" Emmett grimaced at his father, glad to see that he was doing well but upset with what he had to tell them. He sighed, closing his eyes as he mouthed out a response to Seth.

"[I'm glad you managed to care about me, Seth. Isn't it crazy how you're not drunk?]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Emmett was stifling his sorrow, trying to act as familiar to everyone as he usually had.

"[You're acting funny. These guys didn't brainwash you, right? You know that I'm me when I'm most drunk.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" The Llamanian soldiers holding him back let go, knowing Seth would not be a threat.

"[I don't think you understand. You've never really understood the llamanians, or at least never been empathetic towards them. Sure, they’ve made mistakes, but they have always cared for us.]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Seth raised an eyebrow, not understanding his point.

"[Emmett, I watched your fucking parents die. That’s not a ‘mistake’. They aren't trustworthy. You of all people should know this.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}" Emmett squinted at his father, slightly annoyed.

"[I don't care about my parents, Seth. They were drug dealers capitalizing on our people's weak inhibitions. I've been through a plethora of emotions with the llamanians. Even if they were hunting me down, I've always felt close to them since we left Vortox.]{Emmett Tawfeek}"

"[Emmett, for the first time I'm siding with Seth here. Don't be a dick. He's been worried sick about you.]{Sanya Dreadflower}" Sanya put her hand on her hip, trying to conceal the pain Dread was causing her. "[We're not letting these people keep you here and torture you. You’re one of us, we’re not just going to hand you over.]{Sanya Dreadflower}" Sanya was pulling out all the stops she could to get Emmett to get up. Despite the armed guards around them and the massive ship they were in, they could definitely escape if they had put their minds to it.

The throned squoatling chuckled softly, tears flowing from his eyes without his permission. He wanted to look and feel strong in his decision, but it was difficult. He had lived with these people most of his life, and now he had to leave them. His goal of repopulating the squoatling race diverged from their paths today, and he could not bear to say goodbye.

"[Look, I’m safe and sound, and I'm going to be fine. Just not going to be taking any missions anymore. Or… living with you all, for that matter.]{Emmett Tawfeek}" A hush fell among the rabble, leaving a few voices to clearly reply. The fork in the road that was lodged in his throat finally came out. He felt terrible. His mouth quivered as Sanya broke the silence, up in arms, upset and surprised by his response.

"[Wait, you're staying with the Llamanians? But what about us!? You're family!]{Sanya Dreadflower}" Sanya cried out, her flower paining her from the inside. It appears her dread was consuming her, causing her head to throb in pain while her flower bud swelled. Emmett's eyes widened as Sanya held her head, the others huddling around her to make sure she was alright. "[How… How could you LEAVE US?!]{Sanya Dreadflower}"

"[Sanya, you have to realize—]{Emmett Tawfeek}" The llamanian soldiers aimed at the floran as she gave up her anger, as if her roar had exhausted her of her might. Emmett glared at the soldiers gathering behind him. "[Come on, she isn't going to hurt me! Stand down.]{Emmett Tawfeek}"

"[What the hell are you thinking, Emmett? Did you hit your head during their ambush or something? The Llamanians are our ENEMY.]{Garrick}" Garrick pointed an accusatory finger at one of the guards. “[I don’t know what fantasy world you’re living in, but those guys are gonna pull the rug out from under you as soon as you drop your guard.]{Garrick}” Garrick floated above the huddle, trying to get Emmett’s attention. The squoatling hugged his leafy companion, trying to console her.

"[I'm fine. Get off of me, Emmett. You’re clearly going insane. There's no way you want to do this.]{Sanya Dreadflower}" After a minute of silence, Sanya stood, picking up Emmett with her. She knew Emmett did not like this, but for once, he was not complaining about it. He looked over her shoulder, eyeballing Garrick as he spoke to the crew.

"[The llamanians and the squoatlings have lived with one another for centuries in harmony. It's hard for me to hate them for what one member of their species did, even if it was genocide. Maybe it's because I was isolated from everyone, or maybe it's through thousands of years of being culturally close. I don't know. But since they want to make amends for what happened, I need to go, regardless of what I want to do, guys. They're offering me safety in the dangers of the GU, and the potential to find another of my kind. I think finding a mate will be the best for me. I've already caused so much damage from my outbursts.]{Emmett Tawfeek}"

"[We both know your outbursts aren't that bad, Emmett]{Sanya Dreadflower}," muttered Sanya, who was leaning her head on his. This bit of compassion was uncomfortable to Emmett, as it was quite uncharacteristic. However, he remained still, letting her have whatever she wanted of him. "[Please don't leave us.]{Sanya Dreadflower}"

"[With you gone, who's going to be our pilot, anyhow?]{Dakari}" Dakari, having not been as close to Emmett as the others were, was quite unfazed. Bounty hunter groups always changed in their rosters. It was a dangerous occupation, so what was the hold-up? Garrick glared at him, annoyed at Dakari’s failure to read the room.

"[Sanya can manage piloting for us. She's been learning. But still, Emmett, you can't seriously be thinking you'll be in safe hands.]{Garrick}" Sanya was now squeezing the goat’s body a little too hard, so it was a bit difficult to speak with comfort.

"[I'll manage my own safety, Garrick. I've lived alone before. In fact, if they even try to abuse me in any way, I'll manage to escape. They can't afford to lose me though. They're the guilty ones here. I won't forgive them otherwise.]{Emmett Tawfeek}" Seth peered at his adopted son. His trigger finger was shaking, but he understood that there was no way to change Emmett’s mind.

“[Emmett.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}” Seth stepped up to face the kid directly. The others moved aside.

“[Yeah… Seth?]{Emmett Tawfeek}”

“[You know exactly how I feel about the Llamanians.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}” Seth maintained his deadly stare, making it known that he was serious. “[You know they’ve been the biggest force working against us for GUYs.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}”

“[Seth, I know, but are you really—]{Emmett Tawfeek}”

“[But I also know you’re not a kid anymore. I never wanted to admit that, but it’s true. I’ve spent the last twelve GUYs teaching you everything I know about how to survive in this universe. You’ve grown into a man I’m proud to have shaped. So, if you want to do this, I’m not gonna stop you.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}” Seth dropped his glare.

“[…You really mean that?]{Emmett Tawfeek}” Emmett teared up from the sudden affection.

“[I want you to remember something. If you ever believe for a second that the Llamanians are tricking you or doing you harm, kick some ass. Fight for your life. Nobody’s gonna hold Emmett Tawfeek down! The world is your oyster.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}” Emmett, despite Seth towering over him, wrapped his arm around his dad.

“[I won’t let you down.]{Emmett Tawfeek}”

# Chapter 5: The Intercession

After a few tearful goodbyes, a Llamanian officer entered the room from behind Emmett.

“[Excuse me. I’m sorry to interrupt, but we just received orders. Could you all please come with me?]{Llamanian Officer}” The llamanian smiled professionally, motioning for the crew to follow. “[Not you, Mr. Tawfeek.]{Llamanian Officer}” She put out her hand and stopped Emmett at the door. The kid was a bit perturbed by this. What were they being so secretive about?

The remaining crew followed through the long hallway until encountering a large, scary-looking elevator labeled ‘To Briefing Room.’ Garrick chuckled, seeing ‘brief’ and thinking of underwear, which he found funny despite the circumstances. The rest of the crew did not share his sentiment.

“[General Llod will be waiting for you all below.]{Llamanian Officer}” The officer opened the elevator’s doors and stood aside. [*She seriously creeps me out*]{Garrick}, Garrick thought to himself. Nonetheless, all the Pummelers entered the spacious elevator and began their descent.

“[No one gonna talk about this? Why are we being dragged down to this guy’s evil lair?]{Dakari}” Dakari chimed in.

“[Probably going to execute us]{Sanya Dreadflower},” Sanya peered over at Dakari. “[There’s no good reason why we’d be meeting a general.]{Sanya Dreadflower}”

“[Why would they wait to kill us now, though? It must be something more important.]{Iris}” Iris tried to be hopeful, but she was a bit scared.

“[Agreed. We’re not here to be executed, they’re probably trying to get us to ‘join their cause’ or something.]{Garrick}” Garrick looked over at Jess and Volentina, who were visibly distraught about the situation.

“[This is one hell of a way to do it.]{Volentina Constantini}” Volentina rubbed her arm nervously.

“[Well, whatever. We’re not in the holding room anymore, if we wanted to escape we’d just find where they’ve docked our ship.]{Garrick}”

“[Will you all shut up? You’re giving me a headache.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}” Everyone quieted down for fear of Seth’s possibly-drunken wrath. Soon enough, the elevator stopped and the speaker dinged, signaling they had arrived.

The elevator doors opened. The crew stared blankly at the dark room in front of them—it was, indeed, a briefing room, but structured more like a bunker. Past the descending stairs sat a large roundtable with a holoprojector at its center. Screens littered the walls, showing news feeds and strike plans. Guards stood like statues beside the elevator doors, signaling to the Pummelers that they should pass.

Begrudgingly, the crew approached the table, where a Llamanian general stood tall at the end of the table, waiting for their arrival.

“[Vortox Pummelers]{General Llod},” the general said forebodingly as he turned around to face the crew. “[I have been waiting a long time to meet you face-to-face.]{General Llod}” He kept an unsettling smile while he said this, making everyone uneasy and slightly afraid. “[My name is General Llod. Come, sit down, the seats won’t bite.]{General Llod}”

The Pummelers did as instructed, all too weary to oppose the general’s request. The walls clicked to show satellite images of a massive armored space station. The central holoprojector activated to display a 3D map of the base in question.

“[Welcome to the Strike Zone.]{General Llod}” Llod gestured around to the room they were in. “[This is where the Armada plans its attacks. Only a select few are allowed in here.]{General Llod}” Llod clasped his hands behind his back. “[The reason we’ve gathered you today is because, well, we are planning an attack.]{General Llod}” The general’s eerie vagueness was both concerning and very annoying to the crew.

“[Get to the point, Captain Crunch]{Seth Im'Kin'ki},” said Seth, who was not having this today.

“[Of course. We are organizing a strike on a place of particular Armada interest.]{General Llod}” General Llod motioned to a nearby officer, who zoomed into the hologram map. The front screens switched to a new feed, showing a base that sported a corporate-looking emblem. “[This should be familiar to all of you.]{General Llod}”

“[…Oh my God. The Galactic Union?]{Sanya Dreadflower}” Sanya couldn’t believe what she was seeing. The Llamanians had firepower, but even they couldn’t stand up against a force as monumental as the GU.

“[What you’re seeing is the headquarters of the Research, Statistics, Journalism, Education, and Neuroscience Organization, or *RSJENO* for short. It’s a base that is located near the galactic center, and inside is every technological development the GU has worked on for the past few decades. It is the single largest intelligence repository in the whole galaxy]{General Llod},” the general explained. “[This information is vital to the Armada because…]{General Llod}” Llod paused to take a deep breath before continuing, “[We are declaring war on the Galactic Union, and you will be our strike team.]{General Llod}”

The crew was awestruck. A war with the GU spells certain destruction for even the strongest forces. Had the Llamanians gone insane, they thought? No one crosses the Galactic Union and lives, everybody knows that.

“[That’s a suicide mission!]{Garrick}” Garrick exclaimed. “[What, and you really expect us to go along with that?]{Garrick}”

“[I do, and I also expect that you’ll succeed. The Llamanian Armada has had countless encounters with your group over the past few GUYs. We’ve seen your strength and coordination firsthand. Your assault on our mothership seventeen semesters ago was proof of your capabilities.]{General Llod}”

“[We hired hundreds of mercenaries for that raid, and even then we barely managed to scrape out alive. We can’t take on the Galactic Union completely alone.]{Dakari}” Dakari made it out without a scratch, but that couldn’t be said for the others. Most of the mercs were lost trying to get the Pummelers into the mothership, not to mention the crew’s injuries.

“[You won’t be taking anyone on alone. We have been planning this attack for GUYs trying to strategize exactly how we can take that post, and it’s finally time to put it into action. You will have the entire Llamanian military backing you up.]{General Llod}” General Llod yet again motioned for the hologram to change, and it zoomed to focus on a port located on the side of the base. “[The eight of you will be flown here and will dock. Security will be loose here since it’s used to receive shipments. Once your ship has landed, the operation will begin and you all are going to break through.]{General Llod}”

“[Like hell we are. I’ve been through enough shit with the GU. If you all want to kill yourselves for nothing, go right ahead, but I’m having no part in it.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}” Seth stood up and began to walk to the elevator door. The guards were already waiting to block the exit door, rifles in hand. “[Get out of my fucking way]{Seth Im'Kin'ki},” said Seth angrily.

“[I don’t think you understand me, Seth. This is not a request. We are not hiring you.]{General Llod}” Llod adjusted his posture to appear professional and diplomatic. “[The Vortox Pummelers are going to participate in this mission, or we will take you out right here, right now.]{General Llod}”

The guards pointed their guns at Seth, who stood his ground. The entire crew glared at the general with contempt. Seth wasn’t afraid of Llod, and he wasn’t afraid of death. He’d been in worse circumstances than this. He would just come back to life in a few hours, alone, sitting in a cell; all he’d have to do is break out, and…

Of course. That was their edge. Seth wasn’t alone in this anymore. Frankly, he wasn’t too worried about the others, but Emmett… who knows what the Llamanians would do to the kid if Seth blew a hole in their operation. He could be imprisoned, tortured, or worse. Seth couldn’t let that happen, even if it meant joining forces with his worst enemy. As he realized this, two guards approached and restrained Seth, bringing him back to his seat and souring his attitude a little more.

“[I understand that these are not very comfortable terms, but we’re doing what we must to ensure our operation is a success]{General Llod},” Llod explained. “[How does that saying go? ‘The enemy of my enemy is my friend?’ You all have been around the block long enough to know the Galactic Union is too powerful. How many times have GU restrictions gotten in the way of your work? They cover half the damn galaxy! I mean, for Lla’s sake, your captain can’t even pilot because of them.]{General Llod}” He gestured to Seth, who was still not having it; the others, however, began to understand Llod’s perspective. The GU had never been the most sympathetic, and it was due to their negligence that Emmett had a target on his head for these past few semesters. The Pummelers certainly wouldn’t mind if the GU got knocked down a peg, but did they really have to be blackmailed into this…?

“[We’ll do it]{Sanya Dreadflower},” said Sanya, with exasperation in her voice.

“[What!?]{Garrick}” Garrick interjected.

“[Garrick, does it look like we have a choice here? The Llamanians have us wrapped around their little finger. What are we going to do about it? Nothing]{Sanya Dreadflower},” cried Sanya. Her head was throbbing and Dread was fighting her harder by the minute. She was feeling so many emotions at once, and her headache was swelling so much that she just wanted this all to end. “[Let’s just do the mission and get out of here.]{Sanya Dreadflower}”

“[That’s ridiculous. Sanya, you’re just not thinking straight. Back me up here, Seth!]{Garrick}” Garrick was upset and confused by the sudden shift.

“[Sanya’s right. We’re doing the mission]{Seth Im'Kin'ki},” stated Seth emotionlessly. No matter how much it annoyed him, this was his only choice. He definitely wasn’t making his revelation known, though. He had an image to keep up. “[And don’t bother fucking arguing about it, because I’ve already made up my mind.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}”

[*Cold, hard, and commanding as always*]{Garrick}, thought Garrick to himself. [*Are we seriously trapped here?*]{Garrick}

“[Well, Mr. Im’kin’ki, I’m glad you’ve come around]{General Llod},” the general said, very pleased with the change of heart. “[I suppose that means we have an agreement?]{General Llod}” The other crew members looked around, still unnerved. There was a long pause, with nobody feeling confident enough to answer that hadn’t already done so. The room was silent, until…

“[No]{Victor Chomsky},” said Chomsky defiantly. “[Why am I even being roped into all of this!? For the last time, I’m not WITH the Vortox Pummelers. I haven’t been for a long time.]{Victor Chomsky}” Chomsky grimaced, clearly annoyed that his life was still at risk despite breaking his ties with the crew.

General Llod turned slowly and approached the Chromatin. “[Victor Chomsky. Let me tell you a little secret.]{General Llod}” Chomsky’s face changed to one of confusion as Llod grew closer. “[The heirs of the mafia you seized last GUY are back in full swing, and they’re after you. They’d have your head as a trophy if we hadn’t saved your ass. We sent them in the opposite direction when they approached us for information, because you are much more valuable as an asset to this mission. So, Chomsky. You WILL participate in this mission, and you WILL succeed, or else this charade is over and they will rain hell on you and your allies. Understand?]{General Llod}”

Chomsky backed off, still trying to process that he was being followed. After all this time? He was sure his insurrection was successful, that there would be no chance of them coming back… or, at least that’s what he told his people and family.

Garrick approached Chomsky from behind and patted him on the shoulder. The ghost wasn’t sure what Llod’s story was about, but if it meant Chomsky’s well-being was on the line, he might be willing to give this a chance. Despite the distance, they were still friends.

“[Let’s just think of it like… a final send-off. It’ll be like old times. Remember how much we used to goof off on missions?]{Garrick}” Garrick smiled hesitantly. Chomsky did not respond, but the others lightened up a bit from Garrick’s reminiscence. They just had to work together as always, right?

“[I’m glad you’re feeling optimistic]{General Llod},” Llod replied. “[And I’m sure you’ll all feel reassured to know that we prepared upgrades for all of you, to suit your skills. That is, as best the Armada knows them.]{General Llod}”

Llod inputted a code into a holokeypad and triggered a mechanism to the group’s right. The adjacent wall lit up and revealed a massive armory, with compartments for each crew member. The wall was now covered with racks and shelves full of state-of-the-art gear.

“[Whoa…]{Dakari}” gawked Dakari.

“[Copy that]{Iris},” mumbled Iris. “[This is a step up for sure…]{Iris}”

“[As I stated before, the Armada has been planning this mission for a long time. We’ve prepared weapons and protection that are specially designed for each of you. We want the best possible outcome out of this. We’ve optimized each set of gear for your fighting style, body types, team synergy…]{General Llod}” Llod gestured to the display and furrowed his thick brow. “[You would not believe the recon we had to do to get this information.]{General Llod}”

Garrick, as impatient as ever, began to fiddle with his new dual pistols, switching between the many ammo types freely. “[This stuff is high-tech. And it’s light, too. Sanya, try yours out.]{Garrick}”

Sanya donned the knight-like helmet prepared for her. As she suited the gear, fitted with a cloth interior, it began to softly vibrate. “[It’s… actually sort of comfortable.]{Sanya Dreadflower}” She usually avoided headwear due to her flower, but the shape of the headpiece fashioned Dread his own breathing room. Better yet, Sanya realized her headache had been soothed, as well. “[Wait, ‘recon’—you’ve been spying on us?]{Sanya Dreadflower}” She turned to Llod, unnerved.

Seth silently plated his torso and arms with the heavy-duty armor constructed for him. The fit and color scheme reminded him greatly of his God Guard uniform, which the captain appreciated. “[Nice job. Feels authentic.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}”

Everyone seemed pleased with what they were presented with. Though no one trusted Llod, let alone the Armada, it seemed the best option was to play along. After all, they still had most of the crew together. It wasn’t so different from their usual routine.

“[Well… who’s ready for a mission?]{Garrick}” Garrick said optimistically.

“[I’m not a fan of our survival odds. But I have people to live for.]{Sanya Dreadflower}” Sanya muttered the second half under her breath.

“[Hey, cheer up! We’ve gotten through worse than this before!]{Iris}” Iris cheered everyone on, despite the grim circumstances.

The group looked at one another, with some excited, some worried, some hopeful, and everywhere in between. It appeared that, despite the danger ahead, everyone was just as themselves as ever. With Emmett now in safety, the Vortox Pummelers’ longest and most important mission had come to a close. What was left for them now? Could they continue collecting bounties without their shining star? Would they? The thought crossed everyone’s minds, but ultimately, no one worried much about it. The Vortox Pummelers hadn’t gotten this far by fearing the future.

With confidence in his eyes, Seth turned around to face everyone. “[Alright, Pummelers. Let’s kick some ass.]{Seth Im'Kin'ki}”

OVERVIEW

The mission was an overwhelming success. The target location was overtaken in approximately two periods (hours), forty-six unions (minutes), and sixty-one duons (seconds). There were no casualties.

The FINAL PUMMEL squadron entered at 17:34:52 and began the attack. Security was low as expected. The team split into three groups of two with Dreadflower on her own. Im'Kin'ki and Chomsky ambushed the main admin quarters. Garrick and Constantini entered communications and secured the operatives there. Bellatoria and Vatssel shut off power for all pods and docked ships. Dreadflower terminated the security and, despite being alone, held off all defense troops on her own. When LA backup arrived, it was a matter of minutes before the base was entirely secured and the FINAL PUMMEL team retreated.

There was only minor damage to three operatives, all treated on the return flight. Anonymity was kept intact for all recruits, with the exception of Dreadflower, who, after eliminating a fleet of soldiers, removed her helmet to eat the remains while in a “Floran rage state,” as described by Garrick. It is currently unknown if Dreadflower was identified by GU surveillance, but for now, she will remain under Llamanian protection.

The RSJENO base is currently under the supervision of General Llod. All divisions are under Llamanian Armada control. The ports and docking areas have been blocked off to avoid intrusion. All defense systems are reconfigured to eliminate any unsigned ships that approach the outpost.

Mera eroreni Lla sodotaq.
